Hmm, actually — if there's an exception in the script, Streamlit still serves the page but displays the error in the browser. Let me verify more strongly: check whether there are any errors in the complete log (I grepped the full log for traceback|error|exception — none found). But the boundary condition says don't edit files; running a read-only diagnostic command inside the container is fine.

Let me do one more verification: use python from inside the container to fetch the health endpoint, and also verify that the app's source file exists and imports resolve. One more meaningful check: fetch the Streamlit static app assets (e.g. /static/js/...) — not necessary. But run.py only executes when the browser connects (Streamlit runs the script on the first session). The log shows no error at startup, but run.py hasn't run yet.

Hmm, is there a way to trigger script execution without a browser? I could simulate a WebSocket connection… complex. Alternative: verify that the app's python can be imported in the container's environment: `docker exec ... python3 -c "import streamlit; from src.utils.session_state import initialize_session_state"` — but the cwd needs to be /app/blp_streamlit_pipeline. Let me check the app's structure and try importing the main module. This would verify that dependencies are installed inside the image (PaddleOCR, etc.) — a good completeness check.

Let me try: cd /app/blp_streamlit_pipeline; python3 -c "import streamlit, src; ...". Importing session_state may require streamlit's runtime context; safer to just import the package modules. Let me check which modules exist.
